overview: This Senate resolution marks the 30th anniversary of the April 19, 1995, bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City, the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in U.S. history, which killed 168 people, including 19 children, and injured more than 850. It offers condolences to victims' families, thanks the first responders, medical workers, and volunteers who helped, and honors the "Oklahoma Standard" of kindness and service that grew out of the response. It recognizes the Oklahoma City National Memorial and the Survivor Tree, a sapling of which was planted at the U.S. Capitol in 2025. It directs that a copy be sent to the Oklahoma City National Memorial Foundation. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on April 10, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution honors the victims, survivors, and rescuers of a national tragedy and keeps its lessons alive for future generations.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
